what: Authored terminal-status records for census rows, read by scripts/build-registries.mjs. Master prompt section 13.1 requires the actionable-item census to close both ways, and names exactly two escape hatches for a row no rendered control demonstrates: an explicit decision-blocked record, or an explicit not-applicable record. Until audit round 4 finding R4-B05 the generator could emit NEITHER string, so 4,704 rows sat in not-represented, which is neither of the two permitted terminal states, and the escape hatch the section names was unreachable by construction. This file is that hatch.
whyAuthoredRatherThanDerived: A terminal status is a judgement about the source, not a fact the route tree can compute. Derivation is what produces the other three statuses (demonstrated-in-storyboard, mounted-in-another-screen, not-represented) and it is deliberately left alone. What is added here is a record a human wrote, with the four things master prompt section 9.2 requires before a Not applicable classification may stand at all: a reason, an owner, source or decision evidence, and the rows it applies to named one by one.
whatThisFileMayNeverBecome: The number this hatch exists beside is 4,704 rows in not-represented, and the way to make that number small is to relabel it. That is expressly forbidden: an override is legitimate only where the frozen source itself says the row is not a thing a rendered control can demonstrate, or where a named open decision blocks it. After this file, the honest position is still a large not-represented count, and the coverage dashboard publishes it beside the overrides rather than instead of them. tests/coverage/census-closure.test.ts holds both halves.
evidenceLineMeaning: A one-based line number in the frozen source ../AVIIXA_Production_Product_Blueprint.md, sha256 47bd18db467817f3edbe3329c8ae5e332013871aaa2df08c2be6fc5afa8d0b27. Recorded as a bare number with a verbatim quotation beside it so a reader checks the line rather than the record.
whyTheWholeLineIsTranscribed: Audit round 5 finding R5-A06. The gate asserted that evidenceQuote is a substring of the cited line, and it could not see that the SAME LINE'S FIRST SENTENCE describes a rendering that refutes the classification the quotation was chosen to support: line 98508 opens 'In the Super Admin extension screen of section 45A.2, every row in this register renders as a locked entry that cannot be given a schedule.' A twenty-word excerpt of a three-sentence line can support almost anything, so every override now transcribes the WHOLE line into evidenceLineVerbatim, which tests/coverage/census-closure.test.ts compares byte-for-byte against the frozen source, and answers the remainder in whatElseThisLineSays. An author may still make the wrong call; they can no longer make it without the contradicting sentence being in the record and in the diff. R6-C01 then found the second half of the same shape: the record's OWN factual claims were held by nothing. "No page in out/ names a DNC- identifier" was false on the page rendering the sentence. A claim of the form "no page renders X" is checkable against out/, so every such claim now lives in a structured field the gate reads -- see renderedIdentifierClaim.

overrides.reason: §45A.3 is a SCHEDULING-POLICY REGISTER, not an inventory of actionable UI controls, and that -- not any reading of how §45A.2 would render -- is what this status rests on. The section states its own subject: the standing rule is that a scheduled sweeper may assist but must never be the only control protecting safety, authorization, qualification, tenant isolation, evidence or audit, and "Every entry below is an application of that one rule". The register's seven columns are Functionality, Where it lives, Why a scheduled sweeper is the wrong mechanism, The correct mechanism, What a sweeper may still legitimately do, and Source. Not one of them is a control label. The §13.1 actionable-controls census counts 605 distinct labelled UI actions deduped from ControlDefinition labels; a DNC- row names a platform functionality and the mechanism that must enforce it, so that census has no control to count for it. The registry's own countedThing has said as much since the register was first split out: scheduling policy, never an actionable control, and never merged into the 605. R6-C01 CUT THE GROUND THIS REASON USED TO REST ON, and the cut is recorded rather than tidied away. R5-A06 had already removed one overstatement from it. What R6-C01 removes is the sentence that read a locked entry refusing a schedule as an absence of a control rather than as a disabled one, and concluded from that reading that building §45A.2 would turn none of these 22 rows into a demonstrated control either. Read whole, the evidence line says every row renders as a locked entry and that an attempt to attach a Schedule Definition FAILS WITH THE REASON SHOWN, in the same manner the Tenant-Configuration Registry rejects an out-of-bound value rather than accepting and logging it. Whether a rendered row whose attempt fails with a stated reason is ABSENT or DISABLED is precisely the question this build has ruled unsettled at named-test strength: tests/coverage/slice-04-gates.test.ts pins four contested controls with BOTH locator sets and marks the one that is named test against named test as escalated rather than decided. THIS RECORD SETTLED THAT QUESTION IN ONE DIRECTION, AND IT WAS THE DIRECTION THAT KEPT THESE 22 ROWS WHERE THEY ARE. It no longer does. The question is OPEN, is left open, and is cross-referenced to that fixture rather than answered here -- the status does not depend on it, because under either reading §45A.3 is not an actionable-control inventory. The honest correction if the scheduling-policy ground is ever judged wrong is to move all 22 rows to not-represented, not to reword this record.
overrides.owner: JBS build controller, under client approval APP-012 (standing autonomous authority to census closure across all fourteen inventories; where a choice is open, pick what is best for the business and proceed).
overrides.evidenceQuote: On tenant surfaces nothing from this register is visible, because the register describes what the platform refuses to do rather than something a tenant configures.
overrides.evidenceLineVerbatim: **Storyboard.** In the Super Admin extension screen of section 45A.2, every row in this register renders as a locked entry that cannot be given a schedule. Attempting to attach a Schedule Definition to a do-not-use-cron control fails with the reason shown, in the same manner the Tenant-Configuration Registry rejects an out-of-bound value rather than accepting and logging it [SoW Fact — §8.19]. On tenant surfaces nothing from this register is visible, because the register describes what the platform refuses to do rather than something a tenant configures.
overrides.whatElseThisLineSays: The line's first two sentences describe a screen this build does not ship: a Super Admin extension screen at section 45A.2 that lists every row of this register as a locked entry, and that refuses an attempt to attach a Schedule Definition with the reason shown. That is an OWED SCREEN and it is recorded as one here rather than left to be discovered by a reader who opens the cited line. R6-C01: THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO CLAIM "No page in out/ names a DNC- identifier", AND THE PAGE CARRYING THE CLAIM REFUTED IT. Measured over every exported page with the React flight payload stripped, three name a DNC- identifier in text a reader sees: coverage/actionable-controls/index.html names all 22, and coverage/index.html and coverage/scheduled-work/index.html name two apiece. All three publish the census; none of them is §45A.2. The checkable claim is the narrower one and it is stated in renderedIdentifierClaim below, where tests/coverage/census-closure.test.ts holds it against out/: every page naming one of these identifiers is a census publication page, so no shipped route renders this register as a screen. Whether §45A.2's locked entry would render ABSENT or DISABLED is not decided here; see reason.

renderedIdentifierClaim.claim: Every exported page that names one of these identifiers in reader-visible text is a census publication page under out/coverage/, and the actionable-controls index names all of them. That is the checkable residue of the retracted "no page names a DNC- identifier": what is absent from out/ is the §45A.2 register SCREEN, not the identifiers.
renderedIdentifierClaim.howToCheck: Strip <script> and <style> before matching. The React flight payload carries every row id as a key, so a raw grep over the HTML measures the payload rather than the reader -- RESUME section 8, controller defect 9.

decisionBlockedOccupancy.whyZeroRatherThanUnwritten: The status is emittable by exactly the same mechanism as not-applicable above, and no census row qualifies for it today. Measured rather than assumed: the build's decision canon at src/disclosure/decisions.ts carries every open source decision this build met, and each one renders its readings with an adopted, client-delegated position under APP-012 rather than blocking a row. The one item genuinely held rather than adopted is DEC-REPORT-001, which blocks two of MOD-DOH-18's five standard report data sets, and those two are ordinals inside a module rather than identifier-keyed census rows, so no row of the fourteen inventories carries them. Writing an override for a row that is not blocked would be the same defect in the other direction. The coverage dashboard states this occupancy on screen rather than leaving a legend entry that nothing can reach.
